quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition with proper tread depth.
Keep your tires inflated to the correct pressure.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition and properly inflated. Drive slower in the rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at high speeds.

questions.question: What does SATOP stand for?
questions.explanation: SATOP stands for Substance Abuse Traffic Offender Program. People convicted of alcohol-related driving offenses must complete this program.

questions.question: What should you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Move to the right side and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, you must pull over to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the road onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel hard to force the vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and gradually steer back onto the road.
Gently brake to slow down. Turn the steering wheel slowly to get back on the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake to slow down. Turn the steering wheel slowly to get back on the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, slow down gently using the brakes. Once you are at a safe speed, carefully turn the steering wheel to return to the road. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply.

questions.question: What should you do when passing on a multilane highway?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: In Missouri, what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is illegal for an adult driver?
questions.explanation: In Missouri, drivers 21 and older cannot drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Drivers under 21 cannot drive with a BAC of 0.02 percent or higher. A DWI conviction can result in license suspension or revocation.

questions.question: How should a driver treat pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Give the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right to it.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. It is your job as a driver to watch for pedestrians and always give them the right-of-way, even if they are crossing where they should not.

questions.question: Your wheels drop onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car on the road edge.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without hard braking. Then carefully turn back onto the road. Watch for nearby traffic before moving back into traffic.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: What do orange signs mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn about work zones on the highway. These diamond-shaped signs have black letters or symbols and tell drivers that workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: You are in a line of traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle can cross the entire track without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross the entire track without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough room to cross completely. Never pass another vehicle at or near a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any railroad tracks.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is not true?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are best to use on your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter is the hardest driving season and needs extra care. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often. Snow tires improve your vehicle's grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful where children are present. Always let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects how quickly you can stop. Slow down when road conditions are poor to stay in control. You risk losing control if you drive too fast on slippery roads and need to stop suddenly.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and/or flashing lights, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights, sirens, or warning devices approaches, drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle approaching, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Let any emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren pass, no matter which direction it is traveling. Drive to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before stopping on the right.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, you should:

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: If you see this sign, you:

options.text: May pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
May pass if you know the road ahead.
May pass, but only at night.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white rectangles with black markings. Drivers must follow all instructions on regulatory signs. This sign means passing is not allowed.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the other lane is clear.

questions.question: You should honk your horn when you:

options.text: See a child about to run into the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: See a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn drivers or pedestrians who don't see you. For example, honk if a child runs into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: A bicyclist who doesn't obey traffic laws:

options.text: Is correct because bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
Will always get a warning from police.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as car drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: Downward-facing triangular signs:
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. You must let other traffic pass. You can proceed when the road is clear and safe.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to your lane, you may pass:
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line are in the center and the broken line is next to your lane, you can pass if there is no oncoming traffic.
